name: Hogan Butte Nature Park (Volcanic Viewpoint)
tip: The summit lawn of this extinct volcanic vent (about 930 ft) is the best easy Mt. Hood viewpoint on the east side of the metro: Hood sits about 100° (ESE) roughly 58 km away, with St. Helens, Adams and Rainier to the north over Gresham and the Gorge. Go on a clear winter morning for a pink-to-gold Hood especially when low fog sits over Gresham below, or at sunset for alpenglow on Hood while the city lights come on. Park in the 20-space lot on SE Gabbert Rd by the old Brite House and walk the short, steep paved road up; only ADA parking is at the top. Peak-ID signs at the viewpoint help with St. Helens and Adams.
lens: 70-300 for Hood compressed over the Gresham rooftops and for alpenglow details; 16-50 for the panorama of the Cascades over the Columbia; 27 for a clean lawn-and-mountain frame at dusk.
alert: Paved loop is under half a mile; restrooms are seasonal. Check city park hours (Parks Maintenance 503-618-2525) before a pre-dawn visit.
sources: City of Gresham: Hogan Butte Nature Park

name: Tsuru Island Japanese Garden (Main City Park, Gresham)
tip: A small sister-city garden on an island in Main City Park, newly rebuilt in 2025–26 with a bluestone path, stone bridges, bamboo fencing, a roofed entry gate, a boulder water basin and a covered machiai bench. The arching bridge and Japanese maples are the frames. Shoot on soft overcast days in late October to November for maple color without hard shadows, or in spring bloom. The new solar lanterns and lighting are used for evening events such as the October Autumn Illumination, the one chance at a night shot.
lens: 27 for natural, intimate garden frames; 16-50 for the bridge and path compositions; 70-300 to isolate maple leaves against dark foliage.
alert: Open daily sunrise to sunset; admission is free. Renovation was set to finish around the end of September 2026, and the island closed at times during the work, so confirm with the Gresham Japanese Garden before going. Enter from Powell Blvd and Main St, with parking in front of the island. Photo sessions are handled through the garden's rental process.
sources: Gresham Japanese Garden: Tsuru Island renovation updates
